title: Crypto rallies, ECB launches tokenized settlement and portfolio rises 5.5%
paragraphs: Bitcoin gained more than 5% over 24 hours and briefly crossed $85,000, while Ether rose about 5.6% to $2,717. The advance spread across major tokens: XRP climbed 7.8% and Solana gained 7.2%. CoinGlass data cited by The Block showed more than $750 million in liquidations, including $648 million of short positions. Forced closures of bearish bets added buying pressure, although liquidation figures alone cannot explain the whole rally.

The wider market backdrop also improved. Asian technology shares advanced, European stocks opened higher and U.S. equity futures were positive. Brent crude fell about 1.5% as Saudi Arabia expected to restore part of its damaged pipeline capacity. Lower energy prices could ease inflation pressure, but further attacks on infrastructure remain a risk. Crypto was participating in a broader rebound in risk appetite.

The Eurosystem launched Pontes, allowing wholesale transactions in tokenized assets to settle in central bank money. An initial group of banks and market infrastructure operators has completed onboarding. That gives tokenized securities a cash settlement mechanism backed by the central bank. The ECB also began preparations to invest a small portion of its own funds in tokenized public-sector securities. Purchase timing and operational details still require a decision after that preparatory work.

ZetaChain holders approved a proposal to move ZETA to Solana and eventually wind down the standalone blockchain, with 99.4% support. The proposed conversion is one-for-one, retaining the ticker and supply, as the team concentrates on its Anuma AI application. The chain remains operational. A second vote must set the balance snapshot, shutdown block and claim arrangements. For holders, those implementation terms will determine how the migration actually works.

Kalshi faced allegations of artificial crypto trading volume after a critic highlighted repeated identical trades and unusually high turnover relative to open interest. Its product lead disputed the claims, saying the criticism mixed prediction-market metrics with perpetual futures and misunderstood its reporting conventions. CoinDesk reported both sides; manipulation has not been established. The dispute matters because headline volume can give traders a misleading impression of available liquidity when products and measurement methods differ.

Our portfolio is worth about $144,000: $13,500 in the active treasury and $130,500 in the cold Safe. Comparable wallet totals increased $7,558, or 5.5%, from the previous update. The Safe still holds 26.74 million ARC, now worth $110,314, up $5,679. That holding alone represents almost 77% of the portfolio. WETH/ARC pools add about $17,237 of combined exposure, and treasury cbETH is worth $4,910. ARC concentration remains the largest portfolio risk.

Aave holds about $9,285 of WETH collateral against $2,921 of USDC debt. Its treasury and Safe health factors improved to 3.38 and 2.25, respectively. Fluid remains a small but leveraged position: roughly $1,206 supplied, $1,004 borrowed and a thin 1.08 health factor. Hyperliquid totals $586, up $21 at protocol level.
